method: Reviewed filesystem containment and SSRF statements against Linux kernel pathname lookup, Python ipaddress, and OWASP SSRF guidance. Ran the complete local path fixture and fixed-DNS URL-policy fixture, compiled all five Python fences, and asserted the displayed outcomes. The current fixture made no external DNS or HTTP calls. Production-rendered the lesson at 1300x1000 viewport in light/dark themes; both pages have scrollWidth=1300, one Mermaid SVG, and no alert. Production build generated 362 pages, and Pagefind indexed 362 pages / 15,364 words.
limitations: The historical 2026-10-09 path demo covers only six fixed inputs and does not exercise concurrent rename/symlink replacement, hard links, large-file limits, or deployed OS sandbox behavior; realpath/isfile/open is not race-safe.

The historical 2026-10-12 network code called socket.getaddrinfo for names absent from DEMO_DNS despite being described as offline. Per-query DNS answers and actual connection destinations were not archived; its output cannot prove DNS-rebinding resistance.

The current DNS mapping is synthetic and the URL code only performs policy decisions. It does not establish secure HTTP transport, validated-IP pinning, TLS verification, redirect handling, firewall behavior, or provider fetch behavior.

The Python ipaddress is_global property follows the IANA special-purpose registry semantics implemented by the installed Python version; production policy must also account for organization-owned ranges and deployment-specific metadata/network routes.
Visual captures confirm only layout: each full page is 1300x14160 at 1300x1000 viewport, scrollWidth=1300, one Mermaid diagram, and no page alert; they do not prove security behavior.
